plan.new.why: The room's own press makes the plan (`plan.new`, the blank schema or a preset the bundle ships), and it draws only when no plan is open — every capture state sits in a working plan.

apply.why: The batch transport: the OS Plan menu names it and each per-kind paste sheet is its UI form, so no destination capture carries its id.

tx.restore.why: Its declared placement is the palette, which lists every registry command by name (⌘K), and the OS menu names it too — it draws no control of its own until the System surface's Recently-deleted row lands.

record.new.why: The generic spelling: the app dispatches the per-kind New control and the OS menu names the generic id, so no capture renders this id itself.

record.paste.why: The generic spelling, shadowed by the per-kind paste ids the UI dispatches; the OS menu names it.

column.choices.why: The control exists, but a column menu offers it only on a choice column, and no captured state opened that menu on one.

column.reorder.why: The column menu declares it and is its only door — the header's own Move writes the view's columns instead (U5's deliberate deviation).

type.new.why: The sidebar's + menu declares it, reached through the list designer's new-kind mode, and a capture only shows the mode it was opened in.

edit.undo.why: The OS Edit menu bar and ⌘Z carry it; the page answers the key without drawing a control.

edit.redo.why: The OS Edit menu bar and ⇧⌘Z carry it; the page answers the key without drawing a control.

course.paste.why: no preset view of `course` is a cell layout (its screen is a card grid), so the table's Paste control never mounts; the toolbar has the per-kind New, and this id is carried by the palette and the CLI

unit.paste.why: no preset view of `unit` is a cell layout (its screen is a board), so the table's Paste control never mounts; the toolbar has the per-kind New, and this id is carried by the palette and the CLI
